skill.name: configuring-better-auth
skill.description: Guides implementation of Better Auth OAuth 2.1 and OIDC flows for auth servers and Next.js SSO clients. Covers PKCE, JWKS verification, token refresh, logout, client registration, and email verification setup.
skill.summary: Configure Better Auth OAuth/OIDC SSO with PKCE, JWKS, token handling, and client integration guidance.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, OAuth network examples, and configuration environment variables. One static finding is confirmed because the suggested JWKS configuration disables private key encryption. Semantic review also found unsafe auth guidance for token storage, OAuth state validation, callback redirects, and third-party MCP installation; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove localStorage token recommendations and use httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies or another XSS-resistant token storage pattern.
Persist state in a signed cookie or server-side store and reject callbacks where returned state does not match.

remediation.issue: Open redirect risk in callback route
remediation.suggestion: Validate callbackUrl as a same-origin relative path or enforce an allow-list before redirecting.
Remove disablePrivateKeyEncryption or restrict it to local development with a clear production warning.
State that adding the MCP server is optional and requires explicit user approval and provider trust review.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Browser Token Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The auth server reference demonstrates reading bearer tokens from localStorage and later says OAuth clients should only use localStorage. This exposes access and refresh tokens to cross-site scripting attacks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text directly recommends and demonstrates localStorage token use for OAuth clients. Browser localStorage is accessible to injected JavaScript, so this is a clear auth security flaw.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth State Not Verified in Callback
semantic_findings.description: The SSO client creates and stores an OAuth state value, but the callback route only reads the returned state and never compares it before exchanging the authorization code. Missing state validation can enable OAuth CSRF or login substitution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The state value is generated and stored, then read in the callback without a comparison or rejection path. That missing validation is visible in the cited callback flow.

semantic_findings.title: Open Redirect Through Callback Cookie
semantic_findings.description: The callback route redirects to a callbackUrl read from a cookie without same-origin or path validation. A forged cookie could turn the authentication callback into an external redirect.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The redirect target is taken from a cookie and passed into URL construction without an allow-list. The normal setter uses a path, but the server-side route does not enforce that assumption.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party MCP Server Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to add a remote HTTP MCP server hosted at mcp.chonkie.ai. Remote MCP servers can influence assistant context and tooling, so installation requires explicit trust review.

high_findings.title: Crypto seed/private key mention
high_findings.description: disablePrivateKeyEncryption: true, // Disable encryption for simplicity
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly sets disablePrivateKeyEncryption to true for JWKS signing keys. This weakens protection of private signing keys if storage or backups are exposed.

high_findings.title: Insecure Browser Token Storage Guidance
high_findings.description: The auth server reference demonstrates reading bearer tokens from localStorage and later says OAuth clients should only use localStorage. This exposes access and refresh tokens to cross-site scripting attacks.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text directly recommends and demonstrates localStorage token use for OAuth clients. Browser localStorage is accessible to injected JavaScript, so this is a clear auth security flaw.

high_findings.title: OAuth State Not Verified in Callback
high_findings.description: The SSO client creates and stores an OAuth state value, but the callback route only reads the returned state and never compares it before exchanging the authorization code. Missing state validation can enable OAuth CSRF or login substitution.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The state value is generated and stored, then read in the callback without a comparison or rejection path. That missing validation is visible in the cited callback flow.

medium_findings.title: Open Redirect Through Callback Cookie
medium_findings.description: The callback route redirects to a callbackUrl read from a cookie without same-origin or path validation. A forged cookie could turn the authentication callback into an external redirect.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The redirect target is taken from a cookie and passed into URL construction without an allow-list. The normal setter uses a path, but the server-side route does not enforce that assumption.

content.user_title: Configure Better Auth OAuth and OIDC SSO
content.value_statement: OAuth/OIDC setup is error-prone across auth servers, clients, token storage, and redirects. This skill guides Better Auth server and Next.js SSO client setup with PKCE, JWKS, refresh, logout, and email verification patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guide Better Auth OIDC provider setup with PKCE public client configuration.
Outline Next.js SSO client routes for login, callback, session, refresh, and logout.
Provide JWKS-based JWT verification patterns using jose.
Describe OAuth client registration, admin-only registration, and seed-client options.
Show email verification and password-reset provider configuration with SMTP or Resend.
List OAuth pitfalls and validation checks for redirects, consent, and token expiry.
limitations: Does not provision infrastructure or deploy an auth server by itself.
Example snippets need review before production use, especially token storage and callback validation.
Assumes Better Auth, Next.js, and TypeScript patterns.
Third-party MCP setup requires user trust and explicit approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a Shared Auth Server

A checklist for redirect URIs, token expiry, JWKS, and logout.

output: Likely causes to inspect in the refresh route.
A safer server-side refresh flow to implement.

output: Security findings grouped by token storage, redirects, PKCE, JWKS, and email verification.
Specific remediation steps for each risky pattern.

best_practices: Use PKCE for public clients and keep client secrets out of browser code.
Store bearer tokens in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies when possible.
Verify state, redirect URI, issuer, audience, and JWKS signatures before trusting tokens.
anti_patterns: Do not store access or refresh tokens in localStorage for production apps.
Do not skip OAuth state validation in callback routes.
Do not add third-party MCP servers without explicit trust review.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure Better Auth OAuth/OIDC servers and Next.js SSO clients with PKCE and JWKS patterns.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production system?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that still require project-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with token refresh?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes server-side refresh routes, cookie handling, and common failure points.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is the Better Auth MCP server required?
faq.answer: No. The MCP server is optional and should only be added after a trust review.

faq.question: What should teams review before production?
faq.answer: Review token storage, state validation, redirect handling, JWKS key protection, email delivery, and logout behavior.
